lit.'<p>En un <b>borde divergente</b> las pl:
'

At a divergent boundary the plates move apart. The mantle rises, partly melts and the magma builds new crust at mid-ocean ridges, such as the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. Rocks are younger near the ridge and older further away. There are shallow earthquakes and basaltic volcanism (Iceland).

'
lit.'<p>En un <b>borde transformante</b> las:
'

At a transform boundary the plates slide sideways, neither creating nor destroying crust, as along the San Andreas Fault. Friction locks them, they build up stress for years and release it suddenly in an earthquake. There are usually no volcanoes.

'
lit.'<p>Frente a Chile, la <b>placa de Nazca:
'

Off Chile, the Nazca plate (oceanic, denser) slides beneath the South American plate at about 6–7 cm a year: it is a subduction zone. An oceanic trench, the Andes mountains and volcanoes form, because the sinking plate releases water that partly melts the mantle. Friction between the plates produces Chile’s great earthquakes.

'
lit.'<p>La capa externa rígida de la Tierra,:
'

The Earth’s rigid outer layer, the lithosphere (crust and uppermost mantle), is broken into tectonic plates that move a few centimetres a year, driven by convection currents in the mantle and by the weight of sinking plates. Earthquakes and volcanoes cluster at their boundaries.

'
lit.'<p>Un <b>sismo</b> es la liberación rep:
'

An earthquake is the sudden release of energy stored in a fault. The rupture point is the focus (hypocentre) and the point above it on the surface, the epicentre. P waves (primary, longitudinal, ≈ 6 km/s, through solids and liquids) and S waves (secondary, transverse, ≈ 3.5 km/s, only through solids) radiate out. At the surface, surface waves cause most of the damage.

'
lit.'<p>Un <b>sismógrafo</b> registra primer:
'

A seismograph records the P waves first and then the S waves. The further away the epicentre, the longer the delay: d ≈ 8.4 km per second of S − P difference. Three stations locate the epicentre (triangulation). Magnitude measures energy: each extra unit releases ≈ 32 times more energy. Chile recorded the largest earthquake ever measured: Valdivia 1960, magnitude 9.5. Prevention: earthquake-resistant building, evacuation plans and tsunami warnings.

'
